what_happened: All five pinned Lean Challenge signatures were validated at plan-authoring time by 'lean-challenge-snapshot.sh 909 . --dry-run --compile', which elaborated the assembled module against the project's own toolchain and returned 'compile: OK'. Signature well-formedness is therefore not a residual implementation risk; only provability is.

The construction's path-level assembly must land in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderChain.lean, one file beyond the task's declared file_scope (LadderCell.lean, LadderPump.lean), because every piece it consumes (the overshoot loop, hasForwardSlack_raise, anchor_clause_of_first_region_start, exists_deleted_ladderPath_of_pend_past_nxt) lives there and LadderCell.lean's own module contract forbids holding a path-level assembly. Declared in Phase 1's Files to modify; no territory conflict (sibling 915 declares specs/literature-index.json only). LadderPump.lean turns out not to need modification at all.

Phase 1's specified internal spine (copy the landed up-first proof, change the final exists_deleted_ladderPath_of_pend_past_nxt anchor to n0, and thread +k through the overshoot loop's slack bookkeeping) is NOT implementable without modifying a landed declaration: exists_deleted_ladderPath_overshoot_of_pend_past PINS its slack amount to the shape R*l + budget*l at register nxtAt g z, both in hypothesis and conclusion, so the extra k of slack is destroyed by the loop and cannot be recovered (slack transport is exact in both directions). Landed the pinned Challenge signature by a different internal route instead: lower the register BEFORE the surgery via exists_ladderPath_of_walk_nxt_at on the ORIGINAL walk and countdown (anchor clause = anchor_clause_of_first_region_start at deleted length 0, which is exactly where the k is spent), then apply the landed held-register exact-shift theorem to the re-lifted path as a black box. Statement fidelity preserved; decomposition deviates.

The re-lift route (exists_ladderPath_of_walk_nxt_at applied to a path's own walk and countdown with a lowered anchor) turned the register-lowering deletion into a ~70-line reduction to the landed theorem instead of a ~230-line duplicate of the pigeonhole/raise/overshoot/remainder spine plus a generalized overshoot loop. Compiled on the first build attempt.

Phase 2 (retire the landed up-first proof to the k=0 instance) closed [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]: the instance is circular because Phase 1's declaration is proved BY reduction to the landed theorem rather than as an independent copy of its spine. The duplication Phase 2 existed to remove was never incurred. Also recorded: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check could not be run because no challenge snapshot exists for this task.

Phase 1 raised LadderChain.lean's set_option linter.style.longFile baseline from 2300 to 2500 (the module is now 2385 lines). This refutes the 'only additions' half of Phase 1's Scope Hypothesis, recorded in the plan. check-module-invariants.sh treats that set_option as a recorded length ceiling rather than a linter disable, so C29/C30 stayed green.

All five pinned Challenge declarations compiled on the first build attempt in each phase, with no tactic iteration and no new nolints.json row. check-module-invariants.sh (C1-C37) and typst-sync-check.sh were green on the first run at Phase 5, including the C16 env-linter batch and the C34a/C34b marker-honesty constraints.
